environment.description: ECS Fargate service in a private subnet behind an internal ALB. The ALB listener on port 443 is configured with mutual TLS authentication using a trust store sourced from AWS Private CA (ACM PCA). The trust store ARN references a subordinate CA that only issues certificates to the report-scheduler microservice (CN=report-scheduler.internal, OU=platform-services). The ALB forwards authenticated requests to a sidecar proxy (Envoy) which translates HTTP POST payloads into SQS SendMessage calls via the AWS SDK. The SQS queue resource policy restricts sqs:SendMessage to ONLY the task role ARN of the Envoy sidecar (arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/envoy-sqs-publisher-role). No other principal has SendMessage permission. Additionally, the VPC endpoint policy for SQS restricts the sqs:SendMessage action to the same role ARN. The combination means: (1) only the Envoy sidecar can publish to the queue, (2) only requests bearing a valid client certificate from the platform-services subordinate CA reach the sidecar, and (3) only the report-scheduler service holds such a certificate. The report-scheduler performs strict JSON schema validation on the payload before sending (dateRange must match ISO 8601 pattern ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$, outputPath must match ^/data/reports/[a-zA-Z0-9_/-]+\.(?:pdf|csv|xlsx)$).

config.alb_mtls: Mutual TLS with ACM PCA trust store (subordinate CA: OU=platform-services)
config.client_cert_issuance: Only report-scheduler service has valid client cert
config.upstream_validation: report-scheduler validates dateRange (ISO 8601 regex) and outputPath (strict path regex) before publishing
